marquee-vermilion.note: The paper-side red (5.04:1 on #F5F4F3). Never appears on an ink surface.

marquee-vermilion-ink.note: The ink-side red (5.59:1 on #000000). Legal ONLY on the permanent ink surface.

paper.note: The page ground. Warm neutral so a white sheet reads as a separate object on it.

ink.note: Body text, and the permanent black masthead band. Declared at the same value in light and dark on purpose.

sheet.note: Panels and cards — the column of type on the page.

quiet-ink.note: Secondary text at 4.92:1 on paper. Its dark-mode counterpart is #8E8D8B — the two must never be unified.

edge.note: Control boundaries only, at 3.25:1 worst-ground. One value serves both themes. Not interchangeable with Rule.

rule.note: Panel edges and dividers at 1.26:1. Decoration — it is allowed to be faint.

wash.note: Field fills, muted chips, secondary button ground.

cobalt.note: Links, and only links. Lifted to #249BDB in dark, where #14567A is 2.64:1 on ink.

settled-green.note: State, not brand: a week settled, a payment recorded.

caution-ochre.note: State, not brand: a deadline approaching, a slate not yet built.

deep-oxblood.note: Destructive acts. Always as text on a 10% tint, never as a solid slab.

display.purpose: The landing hero's headline and nothing else. Steps up to 6rem above lg.

headline.purpose: The page's subject. One per page.

subtitle.purpose: A panel's own heading. Width returns to 100 here — the boundary between headline and interface.

dek.purpose: The standfirst under a display headline. The one light weight in the system.

body.purpose: Prose, bounded by a measure container (45/65/80ch).

ui.purpose: Every control label, table cell and nav item.

eyebrow.purpose: The kicker above a headline, and the wordmark.

label.purpose: The smallest type in the app. Always uppercase and letterspaced so it survives.

numeral.purpose: Every figure the game produces. Tabular, so columns line up on digits.

numeral-hero.purpose: The one number a screen is about: a bid deadline countdown, a film's score.

shadows.name: raised-object
shadows.purpose: The default Card — the container a poster sits in. Always paired with ring-1 at 5% ink, because a shadow alone is nearly invisible on paper.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, popovers, dropdowns and sheets. These float above the page and must say so.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every interactive focus state. Drawn in box-shadow, which is why the autofill fix never touches box-shadow.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every button on :active, except one that opens a menu. The system's only physical affordance.

motion.name: reduced-motion-collapse
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation still RUNS at an imperceptible duration. Never animation: none — a menu whose animationend never fires stays in the DOM.

motion.name: spinner-reduced
motion.purpose: The one animation that keeps running under reduced motion. It is the only channel a pending action has.

motion.name: skeleton-reduced
motion.purpose: The one animation stopped outright under reduced motion. The skeleton already holds the page's shape and announces Loading.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: The structural break: desktop nav band out, bottom nav and drawer in.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.note: Below this the perforated edge columns are hidden — band content would otherwise paint over them.

measures.name: measure-page
measures.note: The page frame. In rem, not ch, because a page is not text.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The accent control. Reserved for actions that are themselves 'live and yours' — placing a bid, opening a week.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10.4px; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 500; line-height: 1.45; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s ease; outline: none; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, #000); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, #C52F1B); color: var(--primary-foreground, #F5F4F3); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary, #C52F1B), transparent 20%); }

components.name: Ink Button
components.description: Weight without colour. The heaviest control on a surface where the accent is already committed — the correct default for Save and Submit.
components.css: .ds-btn-ink { background: var(--foreground, #000); color: var(--background, #F5F4F3); } .ds-btn-ink:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground, #000), transparent 15%); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The secondary action beside a primary one. Takes the panel border, not the control edge.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: var(--background, #F5F4F3); color: var(--foreground, #000); border-color: var(--border, #DCDBD9); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted, #EDECEA); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Oxblood text on a 10% tint. Never a solid red slab — a destructive act should read as serious, not as the loudest thing on screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, #7A1D10), transparent 90%); color: var(--destructive, #7A1D10); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, #7A1D10), transparent 80%); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The app's field. Bounded by --edge rather than --border, because a control boundary must reach 3:1 and a panel edge need not.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Your bid" aria-label="Your bid" />
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; min-width: 0; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--edge, #84827E); border-radius: 8.8px; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--input, #EDECEA), transparent 50%); color: var(--foreground, #000); font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 400; outline: none; transition: color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s, background-color 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, #6B6A68); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, #000); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--destructive, #7A1D10); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive, #7A1D10), transparent 80%); }

components.name: Flat Panel
components.description: The ordinary panel. If it holds data, it is flat: a border, the base radius, and padding from one variable so header, content and footer cannot drift apart.
components.html:
This week
Bidding closes Friday at 6:00 PM.
components.css: .ds-panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; padding: 20px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #DCDBD9); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--card, #FFFFFF); color: var(--card-foreground, #000); font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-panel-title { font-size: 1rem; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 700; } .ds-panel-body { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, #6B6A68); font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 400; }

components.name: Raised Card
components.description: The artifact container — what a poster sits in. Shadow plus a 5% ink ring, because a shadow alone is nearly invisible on paper.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; padding: 24px; border-radius: 10.4px; background: var(--card, #FFFFFF); color: var(--card-foreground, #000); box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 0 0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1rem; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 700; } .ds-card-figure { font-size: 4.5rem; line-height: 0.82; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 78, "wght" 800; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Ink Masthead
components.description: The top band of every page, signed in or out. The only ground in this palette where the accent is legal as text.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; height: 56px; padding: 0 32px; background: var(--nav, #000000); color: var(--nav-foreground, #F5F4F3); font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-mark { padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 8.8px; color: var(--nav-primary, #EB4B37); font-size: 0.875rem; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 62, "wght" 800; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; text-decoration: none; outline: none; } .ds-nav-mark:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(245 244 243 / 0.3); } .ds-nav-end { margin-left: auto; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; } .ds-nav-item { font-size: 0.875rem; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 500; color: var(--nav-muted-foreground, #8E8D8B); } .ds-nav-item:hover { color: var(--nav-foreground, #F5F4F3); }

components.name: Figure
components.description: A label and its number, stacked — the app's most repeated unit. The numeral is always tabular so a row of them lines up on its digits.
components.css: .ds-figure { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-figure-label { font-size: 0.6875rem; line-height: 1.4; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 100, "wght" 600; color: var(--muted-foreground, #6B6A68); } .ds-figure-value { font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 1.1; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 78, "wght" 800; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--foreground, #000); }

components.name: Perforated Edge
components.description: The brand's signature: 26 x 34 at rx 7, repeated down the inside edge of an ink band. Decorative, hidden from assistive technology at the column, and hidden below xl.
components.html: Opening this weekend
components.css: .ds-band { position: relative; background: var(--nav, #000000); color: var(--nav-foreground, #F5F4F3); padding: 32px 72px; font-family: Archivo, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-perf-col { position: absolute; inset-block: 0; left: 28px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-around; padding-block: 12px; } .ds-perf { display: block; width: 26px; height: 34px; border-radius: 7px; background: rgb(245 244 243 / 0.88); } .ds-band-text { font-size: 1.875rem; line-height: 0.96; text-transform: uppercase; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 70, "wght" 800; }

narrative.overview:
This is Variety for a league of friends. The app reports on a game the way a trade publication reports on an industry: an ink masthead at the top of every page, a paper body underneath it, headlines set narrow and heavy and shouted in uppercase, and figures — box office, Tomatometer, bid, score — set as evidence rather than as decoration. A number in this app is the story. Everything else is the column it sits in.

The material is film itself, but stated as geometry rather than as illustration. A perforation is a rounded rectangle at 26 x 34 with a 7px corner, and that one ratio is the whole visual signature: it repeats down the edge of the ink bands, and it is restated in viewBox units inside the league mark so a league reads as a film cell rather than as a rounded square. There are no photographs of projectors, no reel icons, no grain overlays. The brand is a ratio, not a texture.

Controls are tactile and confident. Buttons carry a wide pill radius and physically push down one pixel when pressed; fields have a real boundary, not a hairline. The app should feel like something you play, not something you file. That tactility is spent on the controls and withheld from the page: panels stay flat, borders stay quiet, and the red is rationed hard enough that when it appears you look at it.
keyCharacteristics: Hierarchy is built from width, not size — one variable family across eleven roles.
Ink and paper are two different grounds, each with its own legal red.
Flat by default; elevation is reserved for things that behave like physical objects.
Numbers get a dedicated type role with tabular figures, so columns line up on digits.
One geometric signature (26 : 34 : 7) carries the entire brand.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: No red is legible on both grounds. --primary is the paper-side red and appears nowhere on an ink surface; --nav-primary is the ink-side red and appears nowhere on paper. Reaching for one on the wrong ground is a contrast failure, not a taste call.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Vermilion means 'live and yours'. It is not the color of a Save button — the ink button variant exists precisely so a screen can have a heaviest control without spending the accent on it. A screen that paints its primary action red has nothing left to mark the open week with.

rules.name: The Ten Percent Rule
rules.body: The accent covers no more than roughly a tenth of any screen. Its rarity is the mechanism.

rules.name: The Sealed Palette Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's stock palette is deleted at the root (--color-*: initial), so bg-blue-500 emits no CSS at all. A raw palette class is impossible here, not merely discouraged. Every color must be a token.

rules.name: The Width Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is width first, size second. Two headings at the same size and different widths are a legitimate distinction here; two at the same width and different sizes usually are not.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any figure that could appear in a column uses the numeral role. A standings table whose digits do not line up is a defect.

rules.name: The Axis Rule
rules.body: Naming wdth in the font binding is load-bearing. Omit it and the loader ships weight-only Archivo, every width distinction collapses silently, and nothing errors.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: If it holds data, it is flat. If it holds an artifact, it may lift. A dashboard of shadowed tiles is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The One Perforation Rule
rules.body: The 26 : 34 : 7 ratio lives in exactly two files — the Perforation component for full-height columns, and LeagueMark, which restates it in viewBox units because a fixed-size div cannot scale into a 26px mark. Never invent a second perforation rhythm.

rules.name: The Circle-and-Cell Rule
rules.body: A person is a circle. A league is a film cell. The shape is the entity type, and it is the brand's geometry doing the work a generic rounded square would otherwise do.

dos: Do cite a token. The stock palette is deleted, so there is no fallback to reach for.
Do pick the red by ground: the paper red on paper, the ink red on ink, never the reverse.
Do use the ink button for the heaviest action on a screen, and keep vermilion for 'live and yours'.
Do set every game figure in the numeral role so columns align on their digits.
Do use --edge for anything a user types in or clicks, and --border only for panels and dividers.
Do build hierarchy by narrowing the width axis before reaching for a larger size.
Do keep panels flat and let only artifacts lift.
donts: Don't ship anything that reads as a generic SaaS dashboard — indigo on white, Inter, large radii everywhere, three KPI tiles above a line chart. That is the default this system was built to escape.
Don't borrow sportsbook language: neon on black, odds flashes, urgency banners, green money glow. This is fake money and a season-long game, not a wager.
Don't hardcode a radius. Every corner derives from the base value, except the perforation's 7px, which derives from the mark.
Don't invent a second perforation rhythm, or draw a league as a plain rounded square.
Don't unify the muted foreground across themes, or treat the nav tokens as a dark-mode variant. The ink surface is ink in both modes on purpose.
Don't add a second <main> inside the shell — every page owns its own landmark, and two fails the accessibility pass on every screen at once.
Don't disable animation under reduced motion; collapse its duration instead.
